annotationRationale: The main work is converting remainder equality into a bounded integer divisibility classification. Factors and multiples support the forced-divisor deductions. The supplied wraparound case analyses are equivalent versions of this route and are consolidated into one complete argument.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Number Theory is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independently, equality requires the divisors of n+1 from 2 through 10 to sum to 9. Only the divisor set {2,7} is possible, giving n=13 and 97. The answer is 2, choice C. The example, choices and key are consistent; no figure is required.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods were supplied. The LIVE explanation and AoPS Solutions 1 through 4 are retained through one consolidated route: divisor sums and wraparound casework express the same remainder-change condition. A separate version would add no useful mathematical approach.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed remainder and integer-solution concepts match the central reduction and exhaustive classification. Factors and multiples appropriately support the forced-divisor deductions. There is no shared-method provenance to inherit.
review.areaCheck: Number Theory is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: For t=n+1, each remainder changes by 1 minus m when m divides t, so the total change is 9 minus the indicated divisor sum. The five listed subsets summing to 9 are exhaustive, and all except {2,7} force an additional divisor. In 11≤t≤100, the seven multiples of 14 are correctly listed and eliminated except 14 and 98.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Both cited references concern this exact question. The sourceMethod accurately consolidates LIVE and AoPS Solutions 1 through 4. The third-party basis is correctly source-informed-original, and the expanded table and explicit exclusions provide independently written explanation.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why differences simplify the problem. The remainder correction, exhaustive subset classification and final finite check are reconstructible. The table explains every nontrivial exclusion.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All three immediate nodes apply: math:modular-congruence covers remainder conditions, math:integer-diophantine-equations covers the bounded exhaustive integer classification, and cnm_p153 supplies factor and multiple reasoning.
